newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill union boss presumed killers - papers.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill union boss presumed killers - papers.

text.p: Algerian forces shot dead the suspected assassins of Algeria's union leader in a "spectacular operation" in which rebels shouted "God is Greatest" in defiance of rockets fired into their besieged hideout, Algerian newspapers said on Thursday.
The newspapers said Algerian government forces killed a "terrorist group" of four men and two women in a guerrilla hideout near the country's main workers' union headquarters in central Algiers.
Two children were also killed in the eight-hour gunbattle, the newspapers said without giving details.

La Tribune said the "killed terrorists" had rented a house in the fifth floor of the 14-storey apartment block overlooking the headquarters of union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda who was shot dead in Algeria last month.

"The terrorists shouted Allahu Akbar (God is Greatest) at the final stage of the raid," La Tribune said. It quoted an unnamed source as saying the guerrillas were believed to be the assassins of Benhamouda, the secretary-general of the Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens.
La Tribune said government troops, deployed on the rooftops of a nearby telecommunication centre complex, fired rockets into the suspected guerrillas' hideout.
Al Khabar newspaper said the suspected guerrillas defied the government forces order to surrender and opened fire on the troops.
"The security forces replied by tossing grenades which exploded inside the flat while some troops stormed it from the roof through the floor above," said al Khabar.
"Six persons were shot dead as well as two children. A third child was wounded," it added.
"The security forces recovered a pair of binoculars and four automatic pistols from the flat," Liberte added.
The Algerian Jihad Islamic Front (FIDA), a small guerrilla faction based in Algiers, has claimed responsibility for Benhamouda's killing on January 28.
But Liberte newspaper said the four men and two women killed in the apartment raid were members of a splinter faction of the the Armed Islamic Group (GIA).
The latest raid followed a wave of massacres and bomb attacks in the past four weeks in Algiers and neighbouring towns and villages in which more than 300 people have been killed.

The government blamed Moslem guerrillas for the killings. About 60,000 people had died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
